newsitem.title: FRANCE: Former Algerian general killed in Oran.
newsitem.headline: Former Algerian general killed in Oran.

text.p: Moslem rebels killed a retired Algerian army general on Thursday in the western Algerian city of Oran, Algerian security forces said.

The Algerian security forces said in a statement on the official Algerian news agency APS that former general Habib Khelil was "assassinated by terrorists", the term they use to describe Moslem guerrillas.
The killing took place in Oran at 1.15 p.m (1215 GMT), shortly after top union leader Abdelhak Benhamouda, who was shot dead on Tuesday in central Algiers, was buried in the Algerian capital.
Interior Minister Mustapha Benmansour called the slaying of the retired general "cowardly" and condemned it "with the utmost vigour".
Security sources told Reuters they believed Khelil was in his 60s and said he had held senior jobs in the army until his retirement in 1986.
Khelil was responsible for army logistics under late president Houari Boumedienne and was director of the army recruitment service under former president Chadli Benjedid, the sources said.

Several senior army and police officers have been killed in the five years of strife between goverment forces and Moslem guerrillas since Algerian authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had a commanding lead.
The army commander of Algiers was shot dead in the capital early in 1995 and an army general was shot dead there later in 1995, the same day Liamine Zeroual took over as elected president.
Former defense minister Khaled Nezzar narrowly escaped death in February 1993 when a powerful car bomb exploded as he drove past in Algiers. He stepped down in 1994.
About 60,000 people have died in Algeria's civil strife since 1992, including more than 170 killed in the past 20 days in bombings and massacres in Algiers and surrounding areas.
